chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of his companions, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Humran and Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal — they both said:

We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no wealth more enriching than the intellect, nor a poverty more abasing than stupidity, nor any backing in a matter greater than consultation in it.'

key_terms.الْحُمْقِ: Humq (stupidity/foolishness) — the absence of 'aql, considered a spiritual deficiency, not merely intellectual
key_terms.الْعَقْلِ: 'Aql (intellect/reason) — in Shia thought, 'aql is considered a proof (hujja) alongside the Imam; it is a divine faculty enabling moral discernment
key_terms.الْمَشُورَةِ: Mashura (consultation/counsel) — Quranic injunction (3:159, 42:38); collective wisdom reduces individual error

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about intellect, stupidity, and consultation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) presents three parallel aphorisms extolling the intellect as the greatest form of wealth, condemning stupidity as the worst form of poverty, and elevating mutual consultation as the best form of support in any endeavor. This teaching reflects the Shia theological emphasis on 'aql (intellect/reason) as a divine gift and a prerequisite for moral and religious accountability, while consultation (mashura) is praised in the Quran itself (3:159, 42:38). The original audience of scholars and companions would have understood this as affirming that true richness is not material but intellectual and spiritual.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Humran and Safwan Bin Mihran Al Jammal who both said,

‘We both heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no richness more enriching than the intellect, nor a poverty more abasing than the stupidity, nor anything more backing in a matter than the frequency of the consultation with regards to it’.
